clue.text: Leaving — one's tired out

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the fodder are rearranged

parts.note: taken as its letters, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone explains they are going because they are worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Desertion is the act of abandoning, a noun synonym for leaving as in 'his leaving the army'.

clue.text: Little Diana, modest but very attractive

parts.note: Di is the short form of the name Diana
a modest person is shy, retiring

explanation.surface: A description of a petite, bashful woman called Diana who is very pretty.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British synonym: someone good-looking is described as dishy.

clue.text: Master taking PE?

definitions.meaning: the captain of a ship is its master
playfully, a person doing skipping exercises in a gym lesson

explanation.definitionFit: A ship's captain is called the master or skipper; a person who skips with a rope is also one, as in physical education.

clue.text: Used by cars and ships in a Greek island, say

indicators.note: say signals that the island's name is spoken and we take a word with the same pronunciation

parts.note: Rhodes is an island of Greece in the Dodecanese

explanation.surface: Traffic of cars and ships on a Greek island, as on Rhodes.
explanation.walkthrough: Cars use highways; 'roads' is also a sheltered anchorage for ships (a roadstead), which is why both vehicles fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Streets are used by cars, and a roadstead or anchorage off shore, also given this name, is used by ships.

clue.text: It's partly a republic, ie country without a king

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the other letters go around the king

parts.note: R is short for Rex, Latin for king
a country is a land

explanation.surface: A sentence about a republic that has no monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: IE and LAND surround R.
explanation.definitionFit: The island is divided: most of it is a republic, the north part of the United Kingdom, so only partly a republic.

clue.text: Words of consolation always matter

definitions.meaning: a phrase said to comfort someone after a setback
a playful contrary: the phrase means 'let it not matter at any time', the opposite of always mattering

explanation.walkthrough: The second half works by contrast: never is the opposite of always, and to mind is to care or matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock phrase used to console, telling someone a setback is not important.

clue.text: Cut down on meat

definitions.meaning: to fell, as a tree, with an axe
a pork or lamb cutlet on the bone

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to fell with blows and a cut of pork or lamb with its rib.

clue.text: One likely to be a responsible person?

definitions.text: One likely to be a responsible person?

parts.words: One likely to be a responsible person?
parts.note: responsible here means to blame, not trustworthy

explanation.surface: Sounds like a description of someone reliable and dutiful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'responsible' suggests dependable; the person responsible for a crime is the guilty party.
explanation.definitionFit: The guilty party is the one held responsible for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Not straight, with future too unsettled

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed, so the letters of the fodder are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: An uncertain prospect: the future looks crooked and unsettled.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from carpentry and engineering for something bent or not exactly aligned.

clue.text: Record the sound of Beethoven's fifth

definitions.text: Record the sound of Beethoven's fifth

parts.words: Record the sound of Beethoven's fifth
parts.note: the fifth letter of the composer's name is H, and to voice that breathy sound is the meaning wanted

explanation.surface: Seems to ask for a recording of the famous Fifth Symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beethoven's fifth' is not the symphony but the fifth letter of his name, H.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics this verb means to pronounce with a breathy H sound.

clue.text: Let Eva twirl in the dance

indicators.note: to twirl is to spin round, so the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tells a partner to let Eva spin during the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballroom dance in waltz time, an old-time British sequence dance.

clue.text: New York politician seen with his extremely beautiful girls

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme letters, first and last, of the next word

explanation.surface: A New York politician is spotted with attractive young women.
explanation.definitionFit: In mythology these are lovely young female spirits of nature, hence beautiful young women.

clue.text: They are empowered to go over our heads

definitions.text: They are empowered to go over our heads

parts.words: They are empowered to go over our heads
parts.note: empowered read literally as fitted with engines, and going over our heads as flying overhead

explanation.surface: Sounds like officials authorised to bypass us and appeal higher up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empowered' and 'go over our heads' suggest bureaucracy, but mean powered flight above us.
explanation.definitionFit: Planes and helicopters are powered machines flying overhead.

clue.text: Hit orchestrated

definitions.meaning: struck successfully, as a goal or a blow
arranged for instruments in a musical score

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both struck home, as a goal or point, and arranged for an orchestra.

clue.text: Knock on a door, perhaps, or the woodwork?

definitions.text: Knock on a door, perhaps, or the woodwork?

parts.words: Knock on a door, perhaps, or the woodwork?
parts.note: knocking read as hammering, as when a joiner knocks a door together or works on timber

explanation.surface: Sounds like knocking at a door or touching wood for luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock on a door' and 'woodwork' suggest visiting or superstition, but point to joinery.
explanation.definitionFit: The trade of making doors and wooden fittings is woodwork.

clue.text: Not functioning properly, being unqualified

parts.note: a computer system that has stopped working is down
done right means done properly

explanation.surface: A machine that is broken and an unskilled worker, both described in one line.
explanation.definitionFit: Unqualified in the sense of absolute or utter, as in a downright lie.

clue.text: Vessels off course?

parts.note: fishing boats using drift nets, and anything carried astray by wind or current

explanation.surface: Ships that have strayed from their route.
explanation.walkthrough: These fishing boats take their name from drift nets, not from straying.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishing boats using drift nets have this name; things wandering off course do too.

clue.text: Exchange hostilities in commercial confrontation

parts.note: to exchange goods is to trade
open hostilities are war

explanation.surface: Two nations swap fire during an economic dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: A conflict between countries fought with tariffs and import restrictions.

clue.text: Doesn't let go — sets free instead

indicators.note: sets free means the letters are released from their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A paradox: someone keeps hold, yet releases instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sets free' rearranges INSTEAD; the surface contradiction is the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone in custody is to keep them rather than release them.

clue.text: He lets loose and is about to curse badly

parts.note: re is Latin for about, concerning

indicators.note: badly means done wrongly, so the letters of the word curse are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man who frees things is about to swear terribly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who saves a person frees them from danger or captivity.

clue.text: Pursued in a persistent way

definitions.meaning: followed closely, tracked like a hound

explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past tense of to follow like a hound, and an adjective meaning tenacious.

clue.text: Officer showing intelligence and real potential

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: potential means not yet fixed, so these letters can take a new order

explanation.surface: An officer shows brains and real promise.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior army rank, among the highest officers.

clue.text: Reprimands for rules etc being broken

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the letters of the fodder are reassembled differently

explanation.surface: Someone is told off for breaking rules and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold someone at length is to give them a telling-off, a verb sense of the word.

clue.text: Old German destroyer still active today!

definitions.meaning: a member of an ancient Germanic tribe that sacked Rome
someone who wrecks property out of malice

explanation.definitionFit: The name of an old Germanic tribe and also a modern word for one who damages property.

clue.text: It's still produced in Russia

parts.note: still read as the distilling apparatus, not as 'continuing'

explanation.surface: Seems to say something is continuing to be made in Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear spirit distilled in Russia, the national drink.

clue.text: A right to be different from others

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A claim to individuality: the right to be unlike everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreign or unfamiliar, as in 'ideas alien to us', a sense of strange.

clue.text: Horses used in a racket

definitions.meaning: the gut or nylon strung across a tennis racket

explanation.definitionFit: The racehorses of one stable form a team of this name, and the cord of a tennis racket is the same word.

clue.text: Support in setting up dinner

indicators.note: setting means arranging, as one sets a table, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Helping out with laying the table for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: to strengthen from below or give foundation to.

clue.text: They are not achieved off one's own bat

definitions.text: They are not achieved off one's own bat

parts.words: They are not achieved off one's own bat
parts.note: off one's own bat read literally in cricket: runs not struck by the batsman

explanation.surface: Sounds like things one did not manage on one's own initiative.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, runs scored when the ball passes the batsman untouched are credited without the bat being used.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket extras run when the ball has not touched the bat.

clue.text: Sailor man in waterproof material

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
Paul is a man's name

explanation.surface: A seaman wrapped in oilskin.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy waterproofed canvas used as a cover, a sheet of tarred cloth.
